svg.aria-label: YouTube Relay Bot high-level design on Huawei Cloud CCE

g.text: Source channel → yt-dlp → YouTube Data API v3 → target channel · Huawei Cloud CCE me-east-1 (Riyadh) · ns relay-bot · 1 pod, Recreate · EVS volume · egress-only via NAT + EIP · Telegram control
ELB or public IP on the node
State on one EVS volume: token,
OAuth done once on a laptop;
Secrets never in git or image;
Hub token only in GitHub secrets
the real ceiling is YouTube, not CPU
Quota spent → run aborts, reports, no retry
same PVC, same token, same IDs
EVS is zonal: pod follows its AZ
No HA by design · volume = single copy
One pod that only dials out
Twice a day (or on /run) the pod lists
videos with yt-dlp and re-uploads them
with the YouTube API. Nothing connects
in: Telegram is polled, every call
leaves through the NAT Gateway EIP.
No Huawei registry: the image lives in
and is pulled through the NAT like any call.
node subnet → EIP · fixed egress IP
every acronym used in this diagram
Data — yt-dlp in · API v3 out
Egress — every call via NAT + EIP
push to main → Actions → Docker Hub :latest/:sha → rollout restart · /run or 06:00/18:00 → yt-dlp → /data/downloads → videos.insert → target channel → Telegram report · state: /data on EVS
Never scale past 1 replica · cloud IPs can hit YouTube's bot-check: smoke-test yt-dlp from the cluster first · OAuth only on a laptop · secrets never in git or the image
